scenes.heading: SHOW IT, *DON'T DESCRIBE IT*
scenes.say: Every agent user knows this: you spend four paragraphs describing what is on your screen instead of just showing it.

scenes.heading: TWO KEYS, *ONE CAPTURE*
scenes.say: Scrawl fixes that with one hotkey. Press Option Shift S, talk and draw over the screen while it records, then paste the bundle into your agent.

scenes.heading: AND IT *ONLY KEEPS WHAT MATTERS*
scenes.say: It saves a frame only when something happens: you draw, you click, or you say look. Each sentence is transcribed on your computer and pinned to the frame it was about, so your agent gets a contact sheet instead of an hour of video.

scenes.heading: BEFORE YOU *INSTALL IT*
cons: Apple silicon Mac, macOS 26 or later
Windows build is an unsigned preview
scenes.say: The honest catch: it is Mac only, macOS twenty six on Apple silicon, and the Windows build is an unsigned preview that does not update itself. In return it is free and open source, and your speech is transcribed on your own machine.
What would you show your agent first? Comment Show, and follow for tools like this.

youtube.title: Scrawl: Stop Describing the Bug to Your AI Agent
youtube.description:
Describing a UI bug to a coding agent takes four paragraphs, and it still guesses. Scrawl lets you show it instead. Press Option Shift S, talk while you point at the screen, and the agent gets only the frames where something happened, with your words timed to each one.

Mac only for now: macOS 26 on Apple silicon. Speech is transcribed on your own machine. Free and open source under MIT.

https://github.com/kitlangton/scrawl
